title: tuesday-kernel-inklings-and-batch-scrimlog
content:
Date: 2029-12-03 (Tuesday)
Facilitator: Maya Hernandez
Attendees: Maya H., Arjun P., Sofia M., Ethan B., Priya S., (notes pulled from post-standup chat)
Location: Zoom + #runtime-kernel Slack thread
Purpose: quick sync on kernel prefill behavior, KV cache stitching oddities, and a short batch-scrim experiment we ran overnight

Top-level summary:
- We landed a small kernel tweak (PR 1874) that changes the prefill->kernel handshake timeout from 120ms -> 80ms for prefills that are tagged "cold-shadow". Early numbers: p95 token latency for short sequences (<=64 tokens) reduced by ~6% on canary nodes; throughput remained flat.
- KV stitching bug resurfaced on mixed-quant models when sequence_length distribution skews > 0.6 toward long-tail (seq > 1024). Root cause narrowed to a race between the eviction scorer and stitcher probe.
- Micro-batching experiment (adaptive split at 12 tokens) increased effective GPU utilization on a throughput-heavy trace by ~7% but introduced jitter in tail latency for smaller prefills; we sketched mitigations.

Notes and observations (raw):
- Kernel tweak (PR 1874) rationale: too many prefills were waiting on a soft handshake when the kernel was already starting warmup tasks. The shorter timeout gives the kernel an earlier hint to either accept the prefill (fast path) or proceed without waiting. Testbed: canary pool c-c11, 8 instances.
- Perf sample (median across 1000 requests):
  - baseline p95 (short seq): 48.2ms
  - after patch p95 (short seq): 45.3ms
  - p50 unchanged within noise floor (~12ms)
  - throughput stable (~same tokens/s within 1.5%)
- Note: these numbers are from synthetic replay trace; real traffic A/B to be scheduled Thur morning.

KV stitching deep-dive:
- Symptom: stitched outputs occasionally contained null KV entries (manifesting as small token dip in probability mass) when eviction and stitch probes collided. Observed more during long-tail sessions.
- Repro: replay with mixed-quant-2 and mixed-quant-3 models, session trace skewed to long sequences (we used user-convo-trace-2029-11-22). Repro rate ~18% of traces under tight memory pressure.
- Hypothesis: eviction scorer computes candidates using a conservative snapshot; stitcher probe runs on a slightly newer head and assumes presence of entries. If eviction proceeds, stitcher exits with partial map.
- Short-term mitigation: add a second-stage verification in the stitcher (cheap checksum probe) to detect missing keys and re-request from shadow-cache. Implemented as hack in canary (branch: stitch-verify).
- Long-term fix options discussed:
  1) Stronger transactional semantics for eviction+stitch (expensive, could regress throughput).
  2) Lightweight lease for stitch requests (preferred: middle ground).
  3) Move stitcher probe earlier in the request lifecycle (needs kernel plumbing changes).
- Action: Arjun to prototype the lease design, target spike by Mon 2029-12-09. Jira: JIRA-ENGINE-4521 assigned.

Batching / micro-split experiment (overnight):
- Experiment objective: reduce wasted fill tokens on short requests while keeping large-batch throughput high.
- Approach: adaptive-split when incoming request token_count <= 12 => route to microbatch path (split max_batch=8). Otherwise use normal path. Also added slight backpressure window of 20ms to let microbatches coalesce.
- Observations:
  - GPU util (night trace): +7% on 6/8 instances.
  - p99 latency variance increased for requests with token_count in [10,15] (they sometimes missed coalescing).
  - Tail jitter correlated with the backpressure window timing alignment; misaligned by ~5-10ms leads to more singleton microbatches.
- Mitigations brainstormed:
  - shift backpressure window to be variable based on recent arrival rate (sliding EWMA).
  - add a lightweight opportunistic sampler to merge singletons arriving within 6ms of each other.
  - route borderline token_count (10-15) into a trial queue that biases them toward the microbatch path during high load only.
- Action: Sofia to land a metrics probe (histograms for coalesce wait times) by Fri 2029-12-06. Priya to run a replay targeting borderline token_count and report sample traces.

Short notes from oncall triage (night shift):
- 02:18 UTC -> transient OOM on node c-c09 (nvlink pressure) while running mixed-quant-3 with prefix caching enabled. Root cause: reactivation of an old memory path in the allocator; fix landed in allocator-refactor branch earlier but not cherry-picked to canary.
- 04:12 UTC -> increased retry rates observed for canary group; correlates with stitch-verify fallback (we were rematerializing keys). Observed ~0.6% higher retries, acceptable for now but needs optimization.

Decisions made in this sync:
- Ship PR 1874 to canary fleet for 24h A/B tomorrow morning; monitor p95/p99 and token-per-request cost.
- Prototype lease-based stitch protection (Arjun). If prototype shows <2% throughput regression, we'll move to an expanded canary.
- Defer heavy transactional eviction work to Q1 2030; prioritize lighter-weight engineering in short-term roadmap.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How much memory overhead will the lease metadata add under worst-case traffic? Rough guess 1-2% but need measurement.
- Does stitch-verify remote re-fetch materially increase request latency for already tail-heavy sessions? We need user-facing replay tests.
- Is adaptive backpressure stable across regionally different inter-arrival distributions? Replay is NA-heavy; need EU test.

Action items (owner — due):
- Arjun: spike lease design + micro-prototype, include memory overhead test (due 2029-12-09).
- Sofia: metrics probe for coalesce wait times + dashboards (due 2029-12-06).
- Priya: targeted replay traces for borderline token_count + report (due 2029-12-05).
- Ethan: cherry-pick allocator fix to canary and redeploy c-c09 (due 2029-12-04) — DONE (see comment in PR).
- Maya: schedule A/B run for PR 1874 (Thur 06:00 UTC) and prepare alert on p99 > baseline*1.12 (due 2029-12-05).

Notes to self / scratches:
- Try alternate name for "stitch lease" — "stitch token" or "murmuration guard" sounded cute in slack, but keep docs clear.
- Keep the canary pool small for now (8 instances) to reduce blast radius.
- Save the long-run transaction design for the infra offsite; this will be a good cross-team session with allocator and SRE.

Reference snippets (for context):
- Quick curl check (local dev cluster):
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"model":"m-q3","input":"hi","max_tokens":32}' | jq '.timing'
  -> {"kernel_ms":32, "prefill_ms":7, "stitch_ms":2}
- Canary log excerpt (stitch-verify):
  [2029-12-03T01:12:06Z] stitch-verify: missing_kv=7 re-fetch-triggered=true session_id=usr-44e

Next meeting: Thurs quick sync for A/B preliminary readouts (2029-12-05 09:00 PT). If A/B noisy, escalate to cross-team triage at 11:00 PT.

End of notes.
